intro: Brussels rewards visitors with medieval squares, Art Nouveau gems and a lively food scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro, tram and bus run by STIB/MIVB; tickets cost about €2.10-2.60 per ride.
Buy a MOBIB card (about €6) or tap a contactless bank card for cheaper fares.
De Lijn buses serve the airport and Flanders; their tickets are not valid on STIB.
Uber, Bolt and local taxi apps work; taxis from the airport cost around €60.
Driving is slow and parking is costly; the low-emission zone covers the centre.
The centre is compact and walkable; shared bikes and scooters are common.

grand_place.name: Grand Place
grand_place.hours: Square always open · flower carpet every two years in August
grand_place.tip: Come early morning for empty photos, then return after dark when the guild houses are lit.

atomium.name: Atomium
atomium.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
atomium.tip: Book a timed ticket online; the lift to the top sphere can queue for 30 minutes or more.

manneken_pis.name: Manneken Pis
manneken_pis.hours: Always visible · small statue in a street fountain
manneken_pis.tip: It is tiny and takes two minutes. Pair it with a walk to Grand Place, five minutes away.

royal_palace.name: Royal Palace of Brussels
royal_palace.price_text: Free when open to the public
royal_palace.hours: Usually open to visitors only in summer · check on the day
royal_palace.tip: The palace interior is only open for a few weeks a year. Check dates before you plan around it.

cathedral.name: St Michael and St Gudula Cathedral
cathedral.landmark: St Michael and St Gudula Cathedral
cathedral.price_text: Free · small fee for the crypt
cathedral.hours: Daily, roughly 08:00–18:00 · check on the day
cathedral.tip: Climb the steps from the lower town for the best view of the facade, then go inside for the stained glass.

cinquantenaire.name: Parc du Cinquantenaire
cinquantenaire.price_text: Free · museums in the park charge entry
cinquantenaire.tip: Walk under the triumphal arch and pick one museum; the park is big and the walk between wings is long.

cantillon.name: Brasserie Cantillon
cantillon.price_text: ≈ €8 self-guided visit with tasting · check on the day
cantillon.tip: It is a working brewery, so wear closed shoes and expect cool, damp cellars. Tastings are small.

cook_book.name: Cook & Book
cook_book.hours: Daily, roughly 10:00–19:00 · check on the day
cook_book.tip: It is a bookshop with themed rooms and a café, not a quick stop. Allow an hour to browse.

duvel.name: Duvel Moortgat
duvel.price_text: Brewery tours by booking · price varies, check on the day
duvel.tip: The brewery is outside Brussels in Puurs. Check train times and book the tour before you travel.

begijnhof.name: Groot Begijnhof
begijnhof.tip: This is a quiet university residence, so keep voices low and do not enter private gardens.

ku_leuven.name: KU Leuven
ku_leuven.price_text: Free to walk the old town · guided tours charge
ku_leuven.tip: Leuven is 25 minutes by train from Brussels. The old university halls are best seen on a short walk.

la_monnaie.name: La Monnaie
la_monnaie.price_text: Ticket prices vary by production · check on the day
la_monnaie.tip: Book opera or a guided tour ahead. The building is also worth a look from the outside.

lions_mound.name: Lion's Mound
lions_mound.price_text: ≈ €10 visitor centre · mound climb may be free, check on the day
lions_mound.tip: It is a battlefield site outside the city. Wear walking shoes and bring a jacket; it is windy on top.

magritte.name: Magritte Museum
magritte.price_text: ≈ €10 · combined tickets available, check on the day
magritte.tip: Buy a combined ticket with the other Royal Museums and go early; the galleries get busy at midday.

moules_frites.name: Moules-frites
moules_frites.hours: Lunch and dinner · mussels best in autumn and winter
moules_frites.tip: Order it in a classic brasserie near Grand Place. Check the price per kilo, as portions vary.

oceade.name: Océade (closed in 2018)
oceade.tip: This water park closed in 2018. Do not plan a visit; check for other pools if you want to swim.

stella.name: Stella Artois Brewery
stella.price_text: Guided tours by booking · price varies, check on the day
stella.tip: The brewery is in Leuven, not central Brussels. Book ahead and allow half a day with the train.

icarus.name: The Fall of Icarus
icarus.price_text: ≈ €10 Royal Museums ticket · check on the day
icarus.tip: The painting is in the Old Masters museum. Ask staff for its room; displays can move.

son_of_man.name: The Son of Man
son_of_man.price_text: ≈ €10 Magritte Museum ticket · check on the day
son_of_man.tip: It hangs in the Magritte Museum. Check it is on display before you buy a ticket, as works travel.

tomorrowland.name: Tomorrowland
tomorrowland.price_text: Festival tickets sell out fast · price varies by year
tomorrowland.tip: It is in Boom, outside Brussels, and tickets sell out. Plan transport and accommodation months ahead.

walibi.name: Walibi Belgium
walibi.price_text: ≈ €45 day ticket · check on the day
walibi.hours: Seasonal, roughly spring to autumn · check on the day
walibi.tip: It is a theme park outside the city. Buy tickets online and go on a weekday to avoid queues.

zoetwater.name: ZoetWaterPark
zoetwater.tip: Details are unclear, so confirm opening and access before you go.

sablon_market.name: Place du Sablon antique market
sablon_market.hours: Weekend mornings · check on the day
sablon_market.tip: Come before noon for antiques and books, then walk to the nearby pastry shops.

mont_des_arts.name: Mont des Arts viewpoint
mont_des_arts.tip: Best city view over the lower town. Go at sunset or after dark for the lit rooftops.

marolles_walk.name: Marolles neighbourhood walk
marolles_walk.hours: Daytime · daily flea market in the morning
marolles_walk.tip: Wander the steep streets below the Palace of Justice and stop at a local café for lunch.

beer_tour.name: Brussels beer tasting tour
beer_tour.tip: Confirm tastings and snacks are included, and eat before you go; Belgian beers are strong.

comic_walk.name: Comic strip mural walk
comic_walk.tip: Pick up a mural map at the tourist office and walk the route at your own pace.

flagey_market.name: Flagey food market
flagey_market.price_text: Free to enter · pay per stall
flagey_market.hours: Weekend mornings · check on the day
flagey_market.tip: A local weekend market with food stalls. Bring cash and go hungry.

styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: Magritte, Old Masters and the comic-strip museum.

stays.why: Steps from the main square, waffle stands and the station. Noisiest and busiest area; book early.
Quiet, elegant streets with antique shops, chocolate makers and the Fine Arts museum nearby.
Local feel, good bars and restaurants, easy tram rides to the centre. Good value.
Close to the EU buildings and parks; quiet on weekends. About 20 minutes by metro to the centre.

food: Try Belgian classics: moules-frites, carbonnade (beef stew with beer) and waterzooi. Main dishes often €15–25.
Waffles come two ways: dense Liège-style and lighter Brussels-style. Street stalls charge about €3–6; sit-down cafés cost more.
Fries from a fritkot (chip stand) with mayonnaise are a local habit, roughly €3–5 a cone.
Chocolate and pralines: compare small makers around Grand-Place and Sablon. Prices vary widely; check the label for cocoa content.
Beer cafés serve hundreds of Belgian beers. Ask for a small tasting glass if you are unsure; strong beers are often 8–12%.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for a half-day trip to Bruges or Ghent by train; check times and prices on the day.
Add the Atomium and Mini-Europe in the north if you want a break from the old centre.
Spend an extra morning at the Royal Museum of Fine Arts and the Magritte Museum in Sablon.
